 356: Ben Bulben is a mountain in County Sligo, north of the town of Sligo. It
is associated with some of the events in the Fenian cycle of Irish mythology,
especially the death of Diarmuid.
 356.1-2: the area around Lake Mareotis (in Egypt, south of Alexandria) is
associated with the rise of Christian monasticism in the fourth century.
 356.3: the titular character in "The Witch of Atlas" (1824) by the English poet
Percy Bysshe Shelley ( 1792-1822).
 356.25-26: in his jail journal (1854), the Irish nationalist John Mitchel (1815-
75) asked, "Give us war in our time, 0 Lord!"
 356.43: the Greek philosopher Plotinus (205-26g/7o), said by Eunapius to have
been born in Egypt. Plotinus argued that art imitates not "natural objects" but
the "Ideas from which Nature itself derives."
